glossary.Bronchi: The large airways branching from the trachea into each lung.
glossary.Bacteria: Single-celled organisms; some cause infections treatable with antibiotics.
glossary.Viruses: Tiny infectious agents that multiply only inside cells; antibiotics do not work on them.
glossary.Risk factors: Things that make a disease more likely.
glossary.Productive cough: A cough that brings up sputum.
glossary.Sputum: Mucus coughed up from the lower airways.
glossary.Shortness of breath: Feeling unable to get enough air; also called dyspnoea.
glossary.Fatigue: Persistent tiredness and lack of energy.
glossary.Oxygen saturation: The percentage of haemoglobin carrying oxygen, measured with a pulse oximeter; normal is 94 to 98%.
glossary.Anaerobic: Living without oxygen; describes many mouth bacteria that cause abscesses.
glossary.Alcohol dependence: Addiction to alcohol, which dulls the gag reflex and raises aspiration risk.
glossary.Foul-smelling sputum: Bad-smelling phlegm, typical of anaerobic infection such as a lung abscess.
glossary.Coarse crackles: Loud, low-pitched crackles from secretions in the airways.
glossary.Confusion: New difficulty thinking clearly; a sign of severe infection or low oxygen.
glossary.Chest X-ray: A plain X-ray image of the chest, used to look for consolidation, fluid or masses.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate test available, against which others are judged.
glossary.Chest examination: Inspecting, palpating, percussing and listening to the chest.
glossary.Penicillin allergic: Having had an allergic reaction to penicillin-type antibiotics such as amoxicillin.
glossary.Supportive: Treatment that relieves symptoms while the infection is cleared.
glossary.Paracetamol: A simple painkiller that also lowers fever.
glossary.Pathophysiology: How a disease disturbs normal body function.
glossary.Alveolar: Relating to the alveoli, the tiny air sacs where gas exchange happens.
glossary.Inflammatory exudate: Protein-rich fluid with white cells that leaks from inflamed vessels into tissue.
glossary.Community-acquired pneumonia: Pneumonia caught outside hospital, most often from Strep. pneumoniae.
glossary.Colonises: Lives on a body surface without necessarily causing disease.
glossary.Lower respiratory tract: The airways below the larynx: trachea, bronchi, bronchioles and alveoli.
glossary.Oral flora: The bacteria that normally live in the mouth.
glossary.Aspirated: Breathed into the lungs, of saliva, food or vomit.
glossary.Cavity: An air-filled hole in the lung where tissue has died and drained.
glossary.Impaired consciousness: Reduced alertness, for example from alcohol, seizures or sedation.
glossary.Antibiotics: Drugs that kill or stop the growth of bacteria.
